### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.test

### Question

Hi there! I already check the other [discussion](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/discussions/1107) but wasn't fully understand.

I am kind of new to neovim plugin testing. Currently I have a basic testing setup for my plugin because most of the time i was testing synchronous functions. Now i move to asynchronous equivalent of what i have before, so the previous strategy will no longer be applicable for new functions.

Here is one of the many asynchronous functions that i have:
```lua
---@param path string
---@param callback function
function commands.touch(path, callback)
  assert(path, "path is not provided")

  local _path = Path.new(path)

  vim.uv.fs_open(_path:normalize(), "a", 420, function(err_open, fd)
    if err_open or not fd then
      return callback(err_open or "Failed to open file")
    end

    vim.uv.fs_close(fd, function(err_close)
      callback(err_close)
    end)
  end)
end
```
Can you provide me an example to test this callback based function. **One more query** which is how to write tests for non-callback based asynchronous functions which means completion cannot be defined.

**If you need more context then here is the [repository link](https://github.com/A7Lavinraj/fyler.nvim)**

comment_data.body:
The answer is indeed the same as in [this comment](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/discussions/1107#discussioncomment-10221879): I usually go with "call the function **in child process**; *wait small amount of time*, validate that it succeeded". I emphasized "in child process" because [this test](https://github.com/A7Lavinraj/fyler.nvim/blob/main/tests/test_fs.lua) doesn't look like it does it. It is not necessary for this question, but it is strongly suggested to do for a robust testing.

So here it might be something like:

```lua
T["touch"] = function()
  local exists_before = child.lua([[
    -- Note, that these are not local, to persist across `child.lua` calls
    -- I'd do this in `pre_case` hook
    Path = require "fyler.lib.path"
    fs = require "fyler.lib.fs"

    -- Make sure that `FYLER_TESTING_DIR_DATA` is assigned *in child process*
    _G.path = Path.new(FYLER_TESTING_DIR_DATA):join "foobar.txt"
    local exists_before = path:exists()
    fs.touch(path:normalize())

    return exists_before
  ]])
  test.expect.equality(exists_before, false)

  -- Wait small time for async function to finish
  vim.uv.sleep(5)

  test.expect.equality(child.lua_get('_G.path:exists()'), true)
end
```

reply_data.body:
Here are couple of observations:

1. Instead of `vim.print()`, use `eq()` (which I highly recommend to create as a shorthand `MiniText.expect.equality`)`. Then running  a test will fail and show (yankable) data you want to see.
2. Instead of `child.lua_get('vim.api.nvim_xxx(...)')` use `child.api.nvim_xxx(...)`.

I don't see an immediate problem with the test case itself. You can use the following tricks to verify that everything works as expected:
- Create and use [`child.expect_screenshot()`](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/6e885e4c27743ae6bf5957ea78ce86c032835f09/tests/helpers.lua#L174-L179) helper to see a screenshot of a child process. If not already, it will create a screenshot file in a 'tests/screenshots' directory. This helps more clearly debug issues that will benefit from visual inspection.
- Temporarily modify your code with log statements and check in the test that everything gets executed as you expect. So:
    1. Add `_G.log = {}` somewhere in the tested code.
    2. Use `table.insert(_G.log, ...)` to append to the log some information to test if this execution path is reached and if it contains data that you expect it to contain.
    3. In the test case use `eq(child.lua_get('_G.log'))` to see the state of the log at that time of execution.

Yeah, deciding on the actual delay can be tricky. On top of that, it might depend on the OS and whether it runs on CI.
There are alternative approaches that basically do "wait until some condition is met" (see `:h vim.wait()` and use it in the test runner instance to check some condition in the child process). But I find them too complex compared to how simple constant delay mostly works.

> * They are failing with same screenshot(of-course hash is not same).
> 
> * I checked the which line is different between `reference` and `observed` but didn't found anything.

Please, read fail messages more carefully. There is always an extra message like "Different `attr` cell ..." which means that screenshots differ by highlighting. In the demo there is something like "Different `attr` cell at line 4 column 35".

Screenshot testing is not broken. There were couple of times they broke after Nightly changes that affect `screenstring` and `screenattr`, but there doesn't seem to be anything like this now.

The reason for screenshot tests to fail is because underlying child process has different screen state to what is expected. Make sure that all conditions are the same. My first guess would be to make sure that running `make` in CLI has the same setup as when running from inside Neovim process.

And no, I will not look at the whole branch with 68 files changed trying to debug this.
